clue.text: Poker and frying pan limiting 100-year piece of nonsense

parts.note: a poker is a person who jabs, so a jabber

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing on both sides, so the pan's letters go round the figure

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese frying pan
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A poker player and a frying pan feature in a century-old bit of silliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poker' reads as the card game but is someone who jabs. 'limiting' puts C inside WOK to make WOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's famous poem of invented words gave its title to any meaningless gibberish.

clue.text: Statesman to talk at length to one acceptable to 20, admitting redtop elevated women-only sport

parts.note: to jaw is to talk at tedious length
a means one

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: halal food is permitted under Islamic law, so acceptable to a Muslim (20 down)
the top of the word red is its first letter

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a hen party or hen night is a women-only event
RU is the abbreviation for rugby union

explanation.surface: A politician gabbles to someone who passes a test, while a tabloid champions a female-only game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' places the red's top letter within the Islamic dietary word; 'elevated' reads the party word upwards. Redtop is also slang for a British tabloid, a false path; 20 down is a believer in Islam.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was the statesman who became the first prime minister of independent India.

clue.text: Agricultural equipment's loose ends in pub

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: a word's ends are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A farm machine has come apart in a public house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes LE from loose, which goes 'in' BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A baler is a farm machine that compresses hay or straw into bales.

clue.text: Site of infection getting payee 2,000 off?

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two thousand is MM

explanation.surface: Is the place an illness started where a recipient of money was cheated of two thousand?
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like a deduction but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Empyema is a collection of pus in a body cavity, especially around the lungs, an infected site.

clue.text: Material set out in program

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: Word is a well-known word-processing program

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fabric is specified in a piece of software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns set into STE, which goes 'in' WORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Worsted is a smooth woollen yarn and the cloth woven from it.

clue.text: Old boy band recording someone else's music

parts.note: cove is old slang for a fellow or chap
a ring is a band, as of metal

explanation.surface: A veteran pop group records another artist's song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old boy band' suggests a group of former pop idols; it splits into Old boy and band.
explanation.definitionFit: Covering a song is recording a new version of music written or first performed by another artist.

clue.text: One dollar 1 across wanting inoculation to show the way to fantastic city

indicators.note: to show is read as to put on display in a new form, so the pool of letters is rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a piece is removed

parts.note: the answer to 1 across, Carroll's nonsense poem
a jab is an injection or inoculation

explanation.surface: A dollar and a nonsense poem minus a vaccine point the way to a magical city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' drops JAB from 1 across, leaving BERWOCKY; with I and DOLLAR it is rearranged. The fantastic city is Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Wizard of Oz, the yellow brick road leads Dorothy to the Emerald City, so it is the route there.

clue.text: Tight corner to fight with energy

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: In a cramped spot one must battle with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward or difficult predicament, a tight spot.

clue.text: 3-D representation of girl consuming tawdry goods

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
tat is cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: A three-dimensional image shows a young woman eating cheap tasteless items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' looks like eating, but it only means the name goes round the cheap goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted three-dimensional figure of a person or animal.

clue.text: Primrose's bovine insolence

parts.note: bovine means belonging to a cow, so cow's (the apostrophe is not a letter)
lip is slang for cheek or insolence

explanation.surface: Someone called Primrose shows the stubborn rudeness of a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: Primrose looks like a person's name with a possessive; it is the flower, and the 's is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a wild flower of the primula genus, a close relative of the common primrose.

clue.text: Compel attention about empty urinal producing stream

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to rivet is to hold someone's attention completely

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something gripping happens around a vacant urinal and leads to a flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' strips urinal to its two outer letters, and 'about' wraps the verb round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivulet is a very small stream or brook, the diminutive of the Latin word for a stream.

clue.text: A tendency to admit Hungary's leader, or Romania's, is revolting

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so these letters are placed inside

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination or tendency

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

parts.note: R is the international vehicle registration letter for Romania

explanation.surface: An inclination to welcome Hungary's or Romania's head of state is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes the first letter of Hungary's; 'to admit' puts that, OR and Romania's letter inside the tendency word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abhorrent is so loathsome it provokes disgust, the same feeling as revolting.

clue.text: Bunch of birds in ruler's domain?

definitions.meaning: a group of birds settled together for the night, as well as their perch
the person who rules the ... is in charge, so the ... is the territory they rule

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second sense: the one who 'rules the roost' dominates a household.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch where birds gather and the idiom of ruling the roost both name this word.

clue.text: Land secured by heiress

indicators.note: secured by means held inside, so the letters sit within the word that follows

explanation.surface: Some territory is kept safe by a wealthy female inheritor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eire is the Irish-language name for Ireland, a country or land.

clue.text: Instructive tale about academic not beyond forgiveness

indicators.note: about means around, so the story's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: a parable is a simple story told to teach a moral lesson
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A moral story about a university lecturer turns out to be excusable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pardonable can be forgiven, so it is not past forgiveness.

clue.text: Popular disc including verse from In the Mood?

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: including means containing, so the disc goes round the other piece

parts.note: CD is a compact disc
a line is a single line of verse

explanation.surface: A hit record contains lyrics from the Glenn Miller standard In the Mood.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Mood is a famous big-band tune, so the clue seems to be about a song; the definition reads it as a phrase meaning disposed. 'including' puts LINE in CD.
explanation.definitionFit: To be inclined to do something is to be in the mood for it, so the word comes from that phrase.

clue.text: Pool ideas of weather-beaten undergarment?

parts.note: a bra is a woman's undergarment
taken as a phrase, weather-beaten describes something caught out in a storm

explanation.surface: A question about what bad weather does to an item of lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a picture: a bra battered by the weather is a bra in storm.
explanation.definitionFit: To brainstorm is for a group to throw out and share ideas spontaneously.

clue.text: Polisher of protective device

definitions.meaning: someone or something that polishes, as with a soft pad
a device that absorbs shock, as on a railway carriage

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a polishing tool and a cushion that absorbs impact.

clue.text: One falling for acrobat

definitions.meaning: a person or thing that tumbles or falls
a gymnast who performs somersaults and flips

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both someone who takes a fall and a gymnast doing somersaults.

clue.text: Girl, 10, changed lock

indicators.note: changed means altered in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ten is the number 10 spelt out

explanation.surface: A ten-year-old girl gets a new look for her hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' is a lock of hair, not a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a curled lock of hair.

clue.text: Stable concern

definitions.meaning: stable means steady and secure, not wobbling
a concern is a business or company

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both solid and steady and, as a noun, a commercial company.

clue.text: Camel sometimes upholds such a believer

annotationWithheld.why: Camel sometimes upholds such a believer (6): MOSLEM is caMEL SOMetimes read upwards, but 'upholds' is both the hidden-word indicator (holds) and the reversal (up), one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Camel sometimes upholds such a believer

clue.text: Last bit of fish? One left

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the last morsel of fish, with only one remaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last bit of fish' wants to give H, the last letter of fish; instead 'Last' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Final means coming at the end, the same as last.

clue.text: Supplies crew garlanding sea dog with noxious plants

indicators.note: garlanding means wreathing round, so the first piece encircles the other

parts.note: to man a ship is to supply its crew, so mans
Sir Francis Drake was a famous Elizabethan sailor, an old sea dog

explanation.surface: Someone provides sailors while decorating an old mariner with poisonous greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supplies crew' is a verb phrase, to man a ship; 'garlanding' wraps it round the Elizabethan captain.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrake is a poisonous plant of the nightshade family, with a forked root of legend.

clue.text: Wordsmith, say, raised amid rubbish

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: eg (for example) is what say means here

explanation.surface: A writer, for example, was promoted amid nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns EG into GE, which goes 'amid' ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mark Roget compiled the famous thesaurus, a master of words.

clue.text: Intoxicant making wound not heal?

indicators.note: wound is read as the past of wind, twisted around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drink that ensures an injury will never get better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but means twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanol is the alcohol in drinks, the substance that makes one drunk.

clue.text: Expression of amusement about one of disgust on electronic channel of communication

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the laughing letters go round the other piece

parts.note: LOL, laughing out loud, is a written expression of amusement
ugh is an exclamation expressing disgust
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Laughter over something disgusting is broadcast on a digital channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel of communication' suggests television, but it is the ear. LUGHOLE is informal British slang for the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear is the channel through which spoken communication is received, a playful sense.

clue.text: Showing restraint when temporal record missing, though formerly included

indicators.note: included means taken inside, so this piece goes into the other

parts.note: a document lacking any record of its time is undated
erst is an archaic word meaning formerly

explanation.surface: Restraint shown when a timeline is lost, though the past was kept in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts the archaic word for formerly inside the word for lacking a date; 'when' and 'though' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something understated is presented with restraint, without exaggeration or show.
